issues.title: Display pipeline stall on memory clock speed change with FAMS2 on gfx1201
issues.author: fililip
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

With high enough display bandwidth requirements to trigger SubVP or DRR SubVP reclocking, memory clock P-state changes (automatic or manual DPM) cause the desktop to stall for a few frames, causing a very visible short freeze, which is unlikely to be desired during reclocking.

This turns out to be a faulty hardware lock introduced in https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/agd5f/linux/-/commit/00c391102abc13763e2bfc90e05503109b19f074, later renamed in https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/agd5f/linux/-/commit/6d92c4d03063480a60bbc3ff61d22197c931f411.

Working around this lock by either removing it entirely or gating it behind a `dmub_hw_lock_mgr_does_context_require_lock` check works flawlessly and eliminates the stall completely: [fams2-mclk-stutter-workaround-minimal.patch](/uploads/09e73a73cacf4c580c8835aceaa574ee/fams2-mclk-stutter-workaround-minimal.patch). I tested this workaround on various different configurations (HDR, VRR, MPO, suspend/resume, hotplugs, etc.) and it never caused any issues. Perhaps it's not needed for dGPUs at all? Especially since without it, SubVP looks like it's doing the correct thing - hiding the clock switch perfectly without any hitches.

Other people report temporary screen blanking rather than stutter on a clock speed change, but it turns out that's due to DRR on some Samsung panels, which seem to blank on VRR on/off transitions. This can be worked around by always setting the `VRR_ENABLED` property to `1` on affected CRT

issues.title: Linux 7.2 AMDGPU Boot/Plasma Freeze on RX 7800XT / RX 9070XT (DCN 4.0.1 / RDNA3 & RDNA4)
issues.author: Rauf Gungor
issues.description:
Building  Linux 7.2 kernel on Fedora 44 with RDNA 3 (RX 7800 XT) or RDNA 4 (RX 9070 XT) graphics cards (two other, RX9060XT and RX9070 are working fine) and experiencing black screen when KDE Plasma / Wayland attempts to initialize (while TTY/Ctrl+Alt+F2 still works), I found the root cause and a hardware workaround.

The Symptom/Log:\
The kernel shows infinite timing controller loops right before the freeze:\
“amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: \[drm\] REG_WAIT timeout 1us \* 150000 tries - optc401_disable_crtc”\
Followed by:\
“workqueue: name exceeds WQ_NAME_LEN. Truncating to: hdmi_frl_status_polling_workque”

The Cause:\
The Linux 7.2 amdgpu module features a severe link-training race condition loop inside its newly rewritten HDMI 2.1 Fixed Rate Link (FRL) status polling workqueue engine when encountering certain monitor HDR metadata profiles. The Output Timing Generator (OTG) gets permanently stuck in a busy loop, locking out Plasma Login Manager Wayland .

The Fix/Workaround:\
Do not use a native HDMI-to-HDMI cable. Instead, use a DisplayPort-to-HDMI adapter (or a native DisplayPort cable) connected directly to the GPU’s DisplayPort output.

By forcing the signal through the DisplayPort protocol pipeline, the driver completely skips the buggy native HDMI FRL polling engine, allowing the display timing registers to pass immediately without hitting the 150k register stall loop. Everything logs in cleanly with HDR functional.

issues.description:
A native OpenGL game (Project Zomboid) triggered a gfx_0.0.0 ring timeout with "Illegal opcode in command stream". The per-queue reset through MES failed ("MES failed to respond to msg=RESET"), the pipe reset is not supported by the CP firmware, so the driver escalated to a MODE1 reset. VRAM was lost and the whole desktop session (GNOME on Wayland) was restarted, killing every running application.

What may be new compared to existing reports: a ROCm compute workload (Ollama, llama.cpp backend, in a Docker container with /dev/kfd) was running a prompt on the same GPU at the same moment. During the reset, the driver also failed to evict and remove the KFD queues ("Failed to evict queue 4", "remove_all_kfd_queues_mes: Failed to remove queue 3", "MES failed to respond to msg=REMOVE_QUEUE"). The ROCm runtime reported "HW Exception by GPU node-1 ... reason: GPU Hang" two seconds after the gfx timeout.

## Hardware and software

- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (Navi 31, PCI ID 1002:744C, subsystem 0x5304, VBIOS 113-D70201-810009), primary display GPU
- Second GPU: integrated Radeon Graphics (Granite Ridge), not used for display
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 9700X
- Distribution: Debian 13 (trixie) with backports
- Kernel: 7.1.8 (Debian package 7.1.8-1\~bpo13+1)
- Firmware: firmware-amd-graphics 20260622-1\~bpo13+1
- Mesa: 25.0.7-2+deb13u1 (radeonsi for the game)

issues.title: amdgpu/DC: EDID override is ignored when a hardware sink's EDID read returns `EDID_NO_RESPONSE`
issues.author: Curtis Vogt
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

amdgpu's Display Core supports the DRM EDID override layer (`drm.edid_firmware` / `edid_override`), but only consults it when it is _not_ doing its own hardware read. When it detects a present sink it reads the EDID over the wire (via `dm_helpers_read_local_edid`), and if that read returns `EDID_NO_RESPONSE` (logged as `EDID err: 2`) it synthesises a fallback mode rather than falling back to the override configured by the user. So `drm.edid_firmware=<conn>:<file>` (or debugfs `edid_override`) has no effect in the scenario where a user would reach for it: a present sink whose hardware EDID read failed. The override does take effect if the connector is also forced on via `video=<conn>:e` or `DRM_FORCE_ON`.

I hit this issue when using a Valve Index HMD, whose EDID EEPROM stops answering after a DisplayPort PHY disable (a headset-side defect, filed [separately](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/SteamVR-for-Linux/issues/939)). However, the behavior is not specific to that device: it affects any AMD user trying to override a bad, empty, or unreadable EDID on a sink that is otherwise present.

## Requested fix:

**Respect the configured EDID override whenever it is set.** When a user has configured `drm.edid_firmware=<conn>:<file>` or a debugfs `edid_override`, DC should serve it and skip the hardware read. To verify the hardware behavior, I created a script that overrides the GPU SSDT via an early-initrd CPIO archive (CONFIG_ACPI_TABLE_UPGRADE):

Extracts & Disassembles: Dumps system ACPI tables and decompiles the graphics SSDT containing Method (ABCL).

Patches Levels: Bumps the DefinitionBlock OEM revision by +1 and rewrites the package returned by ABCL from levels 1..80 to 1..100.

Recompiles & Injects: Recompiles the table with iasl, packages it into an uncompressed CPIO archive under kernel/firmware/acpi/, and sets GRUB to load it on early boot.

The kernel successfully overrides the table on boot. Setting the backlight slider to 100% calls BSET(100), driving the PWM register to 65500 / 65535 (~99.9%) and restoring the panel's full native 500-nit luminance without issues.

issues.title: Skipping device resume in thaw during hibernation is broken/messes with PM state
issues.author: Natalie Vock
issues.description:
On my system, while setting up hibernation, I did some misconfigurations that made the final write of the hibernation image to disk fail.

amdgpu proceeded to explode when aborting the hibernation in that state, which I eventually traced to this patch: https://lore.kernel.org/all/20250710062313.3226149-6-guoqing.zhang@amd.com/

Ever since that patch, the final `thaw()` call before writing out the hibernation image is a no-op. That's fine only when the system actually powers down completely afterwards, but that is by no means guaranteed. When hibernation fails and the system resumes, no separate PM resume function is ever called because as far as the PM subsystem is aware, the GPU should be up and running.

Once userspace is thawed, it tries to submit to the sleeping GPU, everything obviously times out, so amdgpu tries to reset the GPU, which also fails because nothing responds anymore. Bonus points if userspace then crashes, upon which the kernel tries to clean up process resources and meets the same fate (well, it hangs when waiting for PT cleanup fences, but my kernel panics on hung tasks).

If I understand the patch correctly, it tries to work around buffers being moved from swap back into RAM/VRAM even though the system is about to power off, but nop-ing out the entire resume process seems like a quick-and-dirty hack more than anything. Was the actual issue just moving buffers around too eagerly? If so, why not try fixing that instead?

/cc @agd5f @superm1

The MCLK DPM quirk for this board pins the R9 M380's memory to its 300 MHz boot clock:\
measured bandwidth is \~14 GB/s (\~73% of the 19.2 GB/s theoretical peak at 300 MHz on a\

## Summary

When an RDNA 4 GPU (RX 9060 XT, `1002:7590`) is connected via a Thunderbolt eGPU dock, any GPU reset attempt (triggered by GFX ring timeout under 3D load) causes a hard system lock requiring power cycle. **Workaround:** `amdgpu.gpu_recovery=0` — disabling GPU reset prevents the *hard lock* (the CPU hang that follows a failed reset). issues.title: NULL deref in dal_ddc_open (pin_clock->pin) on DP HPD after sink power-down; kworker dies with IRQs off and the machine hard-wedges
issues.author: Dennis T.
issues.description:
## Brief summary

DPMS-off of all outputs, then the monitors drop their DP links. amdgpu handles the HPD as a full `link_detect` / `retrieve_link_cap` and oopses in `dal_ddc_open()`:

```
RIP: dal_ddc_open+0x8c/0x150 [amdgpu]
BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000028
Workqueue: events_highpri dm_irq_work_func [amdgpu]
note: kworker/1:0H[29] exited with irqs disabled
```

`dal_gpio_open_ex(ddc->pin_clock)` returned `GPIO_RESULT_OK`, but `ddc->pin_clock->pin` is NULL. The next instruction reads `pin->store.en` at offset `0x28` with no NULL check. The kworker is killed with IRQs disabled while holding DC AUX/link locks, so the box wedges instead of recovering.

The unguarded deref is still in linux.git `master` (`drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc/gpio/gpio_service.c`).

Call chain:

```
handle_hpd_irq_helper
  → link_detect → detect_link_and_local_sink
  → retrieve_link_cap → dpcd_set_source_specific_data
  → dm_dp_aux_transfer → dce_aux_transfer_raw → acquire
  → dal_ddc_open   ← RIP
```

## Suggested fix

`dal_ddc_open()` already bails if `dal_gpio_open_ex()` returns an error. It does **not** check that the resulting `gpio->pin` is non-NULL before `FROM_HW_GPIO_PIN()`. `dal_gpio_service_open()` would have returned an error if `get_ddc_pin()` was NULL at open time, so a successful open with a NULL pin a few instructions later is a lifetime race (concurrent close vs HPD AUX). The missing guard turns that race into an oops.

Minimum fix — do not dereference a N

issues.title: RX 9070 XT (gfx1201): Ring gfx_0.0.0 reset failed → forced MODE1 / VRAM lost under vkd3d-proton
issues.author: maxivau
issues.description:
**Brief summary of the problem:**

Running a sustained DirectX 12 workload (via vkd3d-proton) on the RX 9070 XT triggers a ring gfx_0.0.0 timeout that the driver cannot recover from with a soft/per-ring reset. The reset always fails (Ring gfx_0.0.0 reset failed, MES(1) failed to respond to msg=REMOVE_QUEUE, failed to unmap legacy queue), forcing a full MODE1 reset, which reports VRAM is lost due to GPU reset!. The desktop compositor (GNOME Shell/Xwayland) loses its GPU context and crashes with SIGABRT, killing the entire graphical session — even though the GPU itself does recover afterward ("device wedged, but recovered through reset").

This is fully reproducible: it has occurred in every sustained session over roughly a dozen occurrences, always exactly once per session, on three different kernels (Ubuntu HWE 7.0.0-30, and mainline stable builds up to 7.2.2). Onset is load-dependent rather than time-fixed — typically 20–90 minutes into a session. One dmesg line points at the likely root cause: The CPFW hasn't support pipe reset yet. — i.e. the current CP firmware doesn't support gfx12 pipe reset, so the driver has no soft-recovery path and must escalate straight to the VRAM-losing MODE1 reset.

- CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor
